questions.question: He left ----- room in ----- fit of anger.[]
questions.explanation: "The" specifies a particular room; "a" is used in the idiom "in a fit of anger."

questions.question: ----- Miles is a popular band in Bangladesh.[]
questions.explanation: Names of musical groups or bands (like the Miles) often take the definite article.

questions.question: Los Angeles has ----- ideal climate.[]
questions.explanation: "Ideal" starts with a vowel sound, so it requires "an ideal climate."

questions.question: A moonlit night is ----- remarkable occasion for a beauty seeker.[]
questions.explanation: "Remarkable" starts with a consonant sound; it is one of many possible occasions, so "a remarkable occasion."

questions.question: ----- man is ----- best creature.[]
questions.explanation: No article is used when "man" refers to the human race in general; "the best" uses the definite article for a superlative.

questions.question: ----- love is such ----- beautiful thing.[]
questions.explanation: Abstract nouns like "love" usually take no article; "a beautiful thing" follows the standard adjective-noun pattern.

questions.question: Outside the bright primary rainbow, ----- much fainter secondary rainbow may be visible.[]
questions.explanation: Introduces a singular, countable noun not previously mentioned: "a much fainter secondary rainbow."

questions.question: Venus is a beautiful planet, perhaps ----- most beautiful of all planets.[]
questions.explanation: Superlatives (most beautiful) always require "the."

questions.question: Suman has ----- terrible headache.[]
questions.explanation: Common health ailments often use the indefinite article: "a terrible headache."

questions.question: Someone, please call ----- policeman to catch the thief.[]
questions.explanation: Refers to any non-specific member of the police force: "call a policeman."

questions.question: I didn't realize how rich he was until I heard that he owns ----- Picasso.[]
questions.explanation: When a proper name (Picasso) is used to represent a work by that person, use "a Picasso."

questions.question: I would like to have ----- piano.[]
questions.explanation: Refers to a singular countable object in a general sense: "have a piano."

questions.question: Which one is correct ?[]
options: What kind of a man is he ?
What kind of man he is ?
What kind of man is he ?
What a kind of man he is ?
questions.explanation: In questions starting with "What kind of," the subject and verb are inverted (is he), and no article follows "of."

questions.question: He began ----- successful career in London as ----- actor, writer and part owner of ----- playing company.[]
questions.explanation: "A successful career" (consonant), "an actor" (vowel), and "a playing company" (consonant).

questions.question:
We must do more to protect ----- environment.
We must fight for the liberty of ----- press.[]
questions.explanation: Specific entities like "the environment" and "the press" require the definite article.

questions.question:
I am learning ----- English.
It's late. Let's go ----- home.
Do you ever have your breakfast in ----- bed ?[]
questions.explanation: No articles are used before names of languages (English), specific destinations with "go home," or the idiomatic "in bed."

questions.question: He went on ----- expensive holiday to ----- Bahamas.[]
questions.explanation: "An expensive" (vowel); names of island groups or countries with plural names require "the Bahamas."

questions.question:
It is ----- pleasure to do business with such an efficient organization.
Last summer we went on ----- cruise in the Sundarbans.[]
questions.explanation: Used in the common expression "It is a pleasure" and for a singular trip: "a cruise."

questions.question: As ----- nation Bangladeshis are ----- religious-minded but not zealots.[]
questions.explanation: "As a nation" is a standard phrase; "religious-minded" is an adjective describing a plural noun (Bangladeshis), so no article is needed.

questions.question: Their car goes 150 miles ----- hour.[]
questions.explanation: "A" or "an" can be used to mean "per." While "an hour" is standard, "150 miles a day/hour" is also a common distributive use of the article.

questions.question: Last year we went on ----- cruise in the Caribbean. Among ----- Islands we visited Bermuda and the Bahamas.[]
questions.explanation: "A cruise" for a singular non-specific trip; "the Islands" is used when referring to a specific group (the Caribbean Islands).

questions.question: It was a beautiful day. There wasn't ----- cloud in the sky.[]
questions.explanation: Used in the negative singular to mean "not even one": "There wasn't a cloud."

questions.question: Kazi Nazrul is ----- Shelley of Bangladesh.[]
questions.explanation: When a famous person's name is used as a metaphor for a quality, use the definite article: "the Shelley of Bangladesh."

questions.question: I think ----- man is very unfriendly.[]
questions.explanation: Refers to a specific man the speaker is looking at or thinking about: "the man."

questions.question: Dairy farming is ----- leading agricultural activity in Australia.[]
questions.explanation: "A leading agricultural activity" identifies it as one of the prominent activities, starting with a consonant sound.

questions.question: Find out the correct sentence.[]
options: A flower is gift of nature.
Flowers are a gift of nature.
A flower is a gift of nature.
The flower is a gift of nature.
questions.explanation: Use "The flower" to represent a whole class or species; "gift" here is a singular countable noun requiring "a gift."

questions.question: Choose the <u>incorrect</u> sentence.[]
options: Nazrul is the Shelly of Bangladesh.
The man speaks English like the English.
Who is more beautiful of the two girls ?
questions.explanation: This is incorrect because the comparative "more beautiful" requires "the" when followed by "of the two" (the more beautiful of the two).

questions.question: Do you have ----- dictionary ? I don't have one, and I need to look up ----- word.[]
questions.explanation: Two singular countable nouns introduced for the first time: "a dictionary" and "a word."

questions.question:
I like ----- blue T-shirt over there better than ----- red one.
She dropped ----- can into ----- grass.
He is ----- best player in ----- team.[]
questions.explanation: Everything is specific: "the blue T-shirt," "the red one," "the can," "the grass," "the best player," and "the team."

questions.question: ----- little learning is ----- dangerous thing.[]
questions.explanation: Based on the proverb: "A little learning is a dangerous thing."

questions.question: ----- burnt child dreads ----- fire.[]
questions.explanation: "A burnt child" represents any child in that situation; "the fire" refers to the specific element of fire in the proverb.

questions.question: ----- Mahabharat is ----- greatest epic in the world literature.[]
questions.explanation: Holy books/epics require "the Mahabharat"; superlatives require "the greatest."

questions.question: Do you sell bananas by ----- kilo ?[]
questions.explanation: When expressing price or measurement units with "by," use the definite article: "by the kilo."
